newsitem.title: CENTRAL AFRICAN REPUBLIC: Bangui president urges army to rebuild nation.
newsitem.headline: Bangui president urges army to rebuild nation.

text.p: Central African Republic President Ange-Felix Patasse on Friday welcomed the return of army dissidents to their units and urged the armed forces as a whole to mobilise to help rebuild the shattered nation.

The disaffected soldiers began rejoining their units on July 10 under a January peace deal brokered by Mali's widely respected former military leader Amadou Toumani Toure to end three army mutinies in under a year.
Patasse, in his first message since the return of the mutineers, offered encouragement to them.

"He asks all elements of the Central African armed forces to mobilise more than ever to rebuild the (nation) which has lived through one of its most seriously crises," his spokesman Prospere Ndouba said.
Toumani Toure returned to the capital Bangui after June clashes between African peacekeepers and army dissidents killed at least 100 people and derailed the January deal.

The mutinies began over pay and conditions but turned into a bid to topple Patasse, a northern civilian elected in 1993. They degenerated in ethnic killings. Most mutineers were from the Yakoma tribe of former military leader Andre Kolingba.
The Red Cross says at least 100 people died in the June clashes and an estimated 60,000 civilians fled the capital.
Under the latest deal Toumani Toure and Jean-Marc Simon, the ambassador of France, the former colonial power, undertook to guarantee the dissidents' security.
France intervened in January under a defence pact to halt fighting and then handed over to the peacekeepers.
